points.zh: 羅莽湖畔《Loch Lomond》，安娜羅荔《Annie Laurie》和我的邦妮《My Bonnie Lies Over the Ocean》都是傳唱已久的蘇格蘭民謠， 每首歌都有人物故事的背景。蘇格蘭高地峻嶺起伏， 山谷翠 綠綿延，湖水掩映，雨霧煙嵐時起時散，清凄幽微的民謠傳說迴蕩其中，自有一縷動人心弦的迷濛詩意。 大學時期的歌本“ 世界藝術名歌 101“ 就收錄了這三首歌。
points.en: "Loch Lomond," "Annie Laurie," and "My Bonnie Lies Over the Ocean" are all long-cherished Scottish folk songs, each with its own story of the people behind it. In the Scottish Highlands, rugged peaks rise and fall, green valleys stretch on, lakes shimmer, and mist and rain drift in and out — within this setting the plaintive, delicate folk melodies echo, carrying their own thread of hauntingly beautiful poetic feeling. During my college years, the songbook "101 Great Art Songs of the World" included all three of these songs.

points.zh: 《Loch Lomond》 ( 羅莽湖畔 ) 是一首傳唱久遠的蘇格蘭民謠，浸染着一段蘇格蘭慘烈的歷史。1745年，以蘇格蘭高地 (Highlands) 氏族為主的Jacobite黨人，第二度大規模起義反抗倫敦朝廷。經過幾回征戰，起初蘇格蘭的軍隊一度還打到距倫敦只有一百三十多哩的Derby，京城倫敦為之震動。但Jacobites黨人於翌年1746年四月，在蘇格蘭Culloden的決定性一役中慘遭殲滅，歷時逾半世紀的Jacobite黨人反抗運動也因此畫下句點。在這場戰役中，英軍把俘擄的蘇格蘭人，囚禁在鄰近蘇格蘭邊界的卡萊爾 (Carlisle)城堡。英格蘭人對待這些蘇格蘭戰俘沒有一定懲處的標準，而是任意挑選，有的處死，有的釋放。據說，蘇格蘭戰俘中有一人預感自己將被處決，寫了Loch Lomond這首歌，託給一位被釋放的牢友，帶回去給他住在羅莽湖畔的情人。這首哀思悲愴，悱惻幽怨的歌謠，就這樣飄盪在蘇格蘭山丘草原，在雲霧繚繞中，綿綿的傳唱至今。
points.en: "Loch Lomond" is a long-cherished Scottish folk song steeped in a tragic chapter of Scottish history. In 1745, the Jacobites, made up mainly of Scottish Highland clans, launched their second large-scale uprising against the government in London. After several battles, the Scottish forces at one point advanced as far as Derby, only about 130 miles from London, shaking the capital. But in April of the following year, 1746, the Jacobites were decisively crushed at the Battle of Culloden in Scotland, bringing to an end the Jacobite rebellion that had lasted more than half a century. In this battle, the British army imprisoned captured Scots in Carlisle Castle, near the Scottish border. The English applied no fixed standard in dealing with these Scottish prisoners, choosing at random -- some were executed, others released. It is said that one of the Scottish prisoners, sensing that he was about to be executed, wrote the song "Loch Lomond" and entrusted it to a fellow prisoner who was being released, asking him to carry it back to his beloved, who lived by the banks of Loch Lomond. This sorrowful, plaintive ballad has drifted ever since across the hills and moors of Scotland, carried on through the mist, sung continuously down to the present day.

points.zh: 《Annie Laurie》（安娜羅荔）是一首膾炙人口的蘇格蘭民歌，旋律優美哀婉，歌詞充滿深情。這首歌的背後有一段動人的愛情故事，與17世紀的一位蘇格蘭貴族女子有關。Annie Laurie（安妮羅荔）是蘇格蘭南部 Dumfries 地區的真實人物。她出生於 1682年，是 Maxwell of Craigieburn 的女兒。傳說她年輕時與一位名叫 William Douglas of Fingland 的青年軍官相戀，但由於門第懸殊，Annie 的父親反對這段戀情，兩人最後未能結成連理。失戀的 William Douglas 將他對 Annie 的愛慕寫成了一首詩，這首詩的第一個版本大約出現在 1700年前後。這段詩後來成為這首歌的核心歌詞。最早的詩歌只有幾節，風格偏古英語。後來到了 19世紀中期，蘇格蘭詩人 Alicia Scott（1810–1900）改寫了歌詞，使之更為婉約通俗，並譜上曲調（或改編自傳統旋律），成為今天我們熟悉的版本。
points.en: "Annie Laurie" is a beloved and widely sung Scottish folk song, with a beautiful, mournful melody and lyrics full of deep feeling. Behind this song lies a moving love story connected to a Scottish noblewoman of the 17th century. Annie Laurie was a real historical figure from the Dumfries region of southern Scotland. She was born in 1682, the daughter of Maxwell of Craigieburn. According to legend, in her youth she fell in love with a young officer named William Douglas of Fingland, but because of the difference in their social standing, Annie's father opposed the match, and the two were ultimately unable to marry. Heartbroken, William Douglas put his love for Annie into a poem, the first version of which appeared around 1700. This poem later became the core lyrics of the song. The earliest version of the poem had only a few stanzas and was written in a somewhat archaic style of English. Later, in the mid-19th century, the Scottish poet Alicia Scott (1810-1900) rewrote the lyrics to make them gentler and more accessible to a popular audience, and set them to a melody (possibly adapted from a traditional tune), producing the version familiar to us today.

points.zh: 《My Bonnie Lies Over the Ocean》 ( 我的邦妮 ) 是一首蘇格蘭民謠風格的歌曲，旋律流暢、朗朗上口。這首歌廣為傳唱，但其背後的起源與故事帶有歷史與傳說的色彩：最廣為人知的說法認為，這首歌與18世紀蘇格蘭王位繼承人查理·愛德華·斯圖亞特（Charles Edward Stuart）——綽號「Bonnie Prince Charlie」有關。1745年，查理王子發起「雅各賓叛亂」（Jacobite Rebellion），試圖恢復父系斯圖亞特王朝對英格蘭、蘇格蘭的統治。在1746年的卡洛登戰役（Battle of Culloden）中失敗後，查理流亡法國，從此離開了蘇格蘭。有人認為，這首歌表達的是蘇格蘭人民對他「橫渡海洋」離去後的懷念與盼望重歸。 雖然這種說法沒有直接的歷史文獻證實，但「Bonnie」在蘇格蘭語中意為「美麗的、英俊的」，又與查理王子的綽號吻合，因此廣被接受。
points.en: "My Bonnie Lies Over the Ocean" is a song in the Scottish folk style, with a smooth, catchy melody. It is widely sung, but the story behind its origin carries elements of history and legend. The most widely known account holds that the song is connected to Charles Edward Stuart, the 18th-century claimant to the Scottish throne, nicknamed "Bonnie Prince Charlie." In 1745, Prince Charles launched the Jacobite Rebellion, attempting to restore his father's Stuart line to the thrones of England and Scotland. After his defeat at the Battle of Culloden in 1746, Charles fled into exile in France and never returned to Scotland. Some believe the song expresses the Scottish people's longing for him after he left "across the ocean," and their hope for his return. Although this account is not confirmed by any direct historical documentation, since "Bonnie" means "beautiful" or "handsome" in Scots and matches Prince Charles's nickname, this interpretation has been widely accepted.

points.zh: 愛爾蘭位於歐洲最西端，本島和離島的海岸線長達五千公里，面積約台灣的 2.5 倍，人口為台灣的 三分之二。景觀豊富多變，自然風光渾然天成，四季變換呈現旖旎各異的綠， 有“ 翡翠綠島“ 之稱。愛爾蘭自古為凱爾特人 ( Celtic ) 居住地  ( Celtic 的發音可以是  Seltik 或是  Keltik ) ， 但屢遭北方來的維京人 ( Vikings ) 的侵犯。現今典藏於都柏林三一學院的國寶“ Book of Kells“，這本西元800年的手抄聖經，被譽為西方書法代表作，就是維京人掠奪焚燒的倖存物。愛爾蘭在十二世紀進入封建社會，下半葉英國侵入，毀其典章文物習俗。1801 年愛爾蘭併入英國，成立不列顛及愛爾蘭聯合王國。1922 年制訂憲法成為共和國，但仍留在英聯邦內，1948年12月21日，愛爾蘭議會宣佈脫離英聯邦，獨立成愛爾蘭共和國。唯北部6郡仍為英國統治，稱北愛爾蘭。1848--1849年間愛爾蘭大飢荒，喪失約三分之一人口，并促成大量海外移民到波士頓，芝加哥等地。
points.en: Ireland lies at the westernmost edge of Europe; the coastline of its main island and outlying islands stretches five thousand kilometers, and its area is about 2.5 times that of Taiwan, with a population two-thirds that of Taiwan. Its landscape is rich and varied, its natural scenery entirely unspoiled, and each season brings its own shifting shade of green, earning it the name "Emerald Isle." Ireland has since ancient times been inhabited by the Celtic people (pronounced either "Seltik" or "Keltik"), though it was repeatedly invaded by Vikings from the north. The national treasure now housed at Trinity College Dublin, the "Book of Kells" — this hand-copied Bible from around 800 AD, hailed as a masterpiece of Western calligraphy — is a survivor of Viking plunder and burning. Ireland entered feudal society in the 12th century; in its latter half England invaded and destroyed its institutions, records, and customs. In 1801 Ireland was incorporated into Britain, forming the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland. In 1922 it adopted a constitution and became a republic, though it remained within the British Commonwealth; on December 21, 1948, the Irish parliament declared its withdrawal from the Commonwealth, becoming the independent Republic of Ireland. The six northern counties, however, remained under British rule and are called Northern Ireland. The Great Irish Famine of 1848–1849 caused the loss of about one-third of the population and drove large-scale emigration overseas to places such as Boston and Chicago.

points.zh: 亞歷山大 . 佛萊明  ( Alexander Fleming，1881—1955 ) ，蘇格蘭人，生物學家和葯理學家，在 1928年從細菌培養皿中發現了青黴素 ( 盤尼西林 )，這是 20 世紀醫學史上，最重要的成就之一。他的發現促使生物化學醫療進入一個嶄新的紀元。1945年榮獲諾貝爾的生理醫學獎。當所有的榮耀逐漸加諸他身上時，他卻謙卑，平淡地說“  我并没有做什麼事，是自然製造了盤尼西林，我只是偶然發現它而已。”
points.en: Alexander Fleming (1881-1955), a Scottish biologist and pharmacologist, discovered penicillin in a bacterial culture dish in 1928 -- one of the most important achievements in 20th-century medical history. His discovery ushered biochemical medicine into a brand-new era. In 1945 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. As honors gradually accumulated upon him, he humbly and plainly said, "I did not do anything. Nature made penicillin; I merely discovered it by chance."

points.zh:
戴維 . 李文斯頓  ( David Livingstone，1813—1873 ) ，蘇格蘭人， 一生以醫生和傳教士身份，致力向非洲土著做醫療傳道事工。也是非洲最偉大探險家之一 ，維多利亞瀑布和馬拉維湖的發現者。被稱為“ 非洲之父“。死後，其心臟埋藏於非洲土地。李文斯頓啟開了英國海外醫療傳道的風潮，其影響遍及全球。同是蘇格蘭人的蘭醫生父子  ( 蘭大衛和蘭大弼 ) ，也是受李文斯頓的精神感召，不約而同的成為醫療宣教士，來到台灣，創設“ 彰化基督教醫院“。在台灣七十年的醫療傳道生涯，為台灣留下了“ 切膚之愛“ 和“ 洗腳精神“，成為台灣醫療奉献的典範，以及信仰實踐的楷模。
Bonnie Banks o' Loch Lomond   - 羅莽湖邊
points.en:
David Livingstone (1813–1873), a Scotsman, devoted his life as both a doctor and a missionary to medical mission work among the peoples of Africa. He was also one of Africa's greatest explorers, discoverer of Victoria Falls and Lake Malawi, and was called the "Father of Africa." After his death, his heart was buried in African soil. Livingstone set off the wave of British overseas medical mission work, whose influence spread across the globe. Fellow Scotsmen, the Doctors Landsborough (David Landsborough III and David Landsborough IV, father and son), likewise moved by Livingstone's spirit, independently became medical missionaries and came to Taiwan, founding Changhua Christian Hospital. Over seventy years of medical mission work in Taiwan, they left behind the "love that touches the skin" and the "spirit of foot-washing," becoming a model of medical dedication in Taiwan and an exemplar of faith put into practice.
Bonnie Banks o' Loch Lomond — the shores of Loch Lomond

zh: My bonnie lies over the ocean   - 我的邦妮
en: My bonnie lies over the ocean   - My Bonnie

points.zh:
從高中時代起，便很喜歡這首蘇格蘭民謠《羅莽湖畔》，一直只當是描述山嶺湖水以及情人離別的歌。自從對歌曲背景及塞爾特人的歷史有更多瞭解後，獨自啍唱或靜聽這首古老的情歌時，心中總浮起陣陣波濤， 在抒情之中，參雜著對遙遠國度那份悲愁的歷史情緒，也感染着塞爾特人堅忍卓絶的民族毅力。
“ 羅莽湖畔“  的歌詞如下 : “ 出城郊  , 風光好 , 望遠坡 , 真美麗 , 香塵日照裡  , 羅莽湖畔  , 憶當初  , 雙情侶  , 終朝攜手共遊戲  , 在那美麗美麗的羅莽湖畔。你要越高山  , 我要屨平夷  , 到鄉關行路難  , 你來何遲  , 哦  , 哦  , 雙情侶從今恐無相見期  , 在那美麗美麗的羅莽湖畔。”
“ 安娜羅荔“  的歌詞如下 : “ 美麗的麥威頓坡 , 坡上新露清淒  , 在那裡  , 安娜羅荔給我難忘的信誓 , 她說永不分離 , 我說永不相背 , 為著可愛的安娜羅荔  , 我的心至死不移。”
points.en:
Since high school I have loved the Scottish folk song 'The Bonnie Banks o' Loch Lomond,' and for a long time took it simply as a song about mountains, lakes, and a parting of lovers. After coming to know more about the song's background and the history of the Celtic people, whenever I hum it alone or listen to it quietly, this old love song stirs waves in my heart — amid its lyricism mingles a sorrowful historical emotion for a distant land, and it also conveys something of the tenacious, unyielding will of the Celtic people.
The lyrics of 'Loch Lomond' are as follows: 'By yon bonnie banks and by yon bonnie braes, where the sun shines bright on Loch Lomond, where me and my true love were ever wont to gae, on the bonnie, bonnie banks of Loch Lomond. You take the high road and I'll take the low road, and I'll be in Scotland before you; but me and my true love will never meet again, on the bonnie, bonnie banks of Loch Lomond.'
The lyrics of 'Annie Laurie' are as follows: 'Maxwelton's braes are bonnie, where early fa's the dew, and it's there that Annie Laurie gave me her promise true — gave me her promise true, which ne'er forgot will be; and for bonnie Annie Laurie I'd lay me doon and dee.'
